newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares soar 3.61 pct on cash entry.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares soar 3.61 pct on cash entry.

text.p: Istanbul shares surged nearly four percent amid fresh liquidity inflow on Tuesday although caution caused by political uncertainty continued, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed 53 points, or 3.61 percent higher at 1,523 after edging up 0.2 percent on Monday. Trade volume jumped to 19.90 trillion lira ($142.5 million) from yesterday's 13.43 trillion ($96.4 million).
Brokers said the index eased briefly on profit-taking in the afternoon following a 3.27 percent gain in the morning when it pierced the 1,500 resistance and targeted 1,525.
"Direction will become clearer after news to emerge from today's cabinet meeting," said Tuncay Kuzu from Sahin securities.
The Islamist-led coalition will hold its first cabinet meeting in eight weeks on Tuesday evening amidst a continuing row with the secularist establishment.
A deepening rift between Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamists and the conservative, pro-Western wing of the coalition had forced the cancellation of a string of weekly meetings.
Brokers said press reports about Erbakan agreeing to an army plan to sack scores of Islamist soldiers at Tuesday's Supreme Military Council meeting also supported today's early buying.

The coalition has been ailing since a February National Security Council (NSC) meeting where the secularist military demanded that the government take a list of measures to fight rising Islamist zeal.
